key_insight: Standardising EHR data to OMOP improved interoperability and allowed a clinical language model trained on one UK primary care dataset to transfer well to another.
clinical_relevance: This suggests hospitals and health systems may reuse clinical language models across differently structured EHR datasets after common-data-model mapping.
method: Mapped two UK primary care datasets (CPRD GOLD and CPRD Aurum) to OMOP standard concepts.
Pretrained a BERT-based transformer on GOLD and fine-tuned it separately on both datasets.
Evaluated prediction of 30-day emergency hospital readmission and ran ablation tests on major OMOP domains.
evidence_signal: OMOP mapping covered 95.6% of GOLD records and 86.2% of Aurum records; Aurum fine-tuning reached AUC 0.93 versus 0.91 for GOLD.
watch_item: Incomplete vocabulary coverage and dataset-specific differences in data structure may limit portability and cause information loss in real-world deployment.
paper_title: Interoperability of standardised electronic healthcare records facilitates transfer learning of clinical language models
